65	7. **Script nodes must `return` an object** — `return { key: value }`, not a bare scalar.
66	8. **Validate once at the end** — run `uip maestro flow validate` only after all nodes, edges, and configuration are complete. Do not validate after each individual node add or edit — intermediate states are expected to be invalid.

112	## Anti-patterns
113	
114	- **Prefer running `uip maestro flow init` from inside the solution you named** — run outside one it auto-scaffolds `<Project>Solution/`, but the auto name won't match your chosen solution name. Never pass `--skip-solution-registration` for a project you intend to upload (it leaves a bare single-nested layout). See [SKILL.md rule #6](../../SKILL.md#critical-rules-universal) for the required double-nested `<Solution>/<Project>/<Project>.flow` layout and the self-check.
115	- **Never guess node schemas** — use `registry get` for all node types. Guessed port names or input fields cause silent wiring failures.
116	- **Never skip capability discovery for connector nodes** — run `registry search` to confirm the connector exists and what operations it supports before building. See [connector/planning.md](references/plugins/connector/planning.md). Skipping this is the #1 cause of designing around a connector that doesn't exist or an operation it doesn't support.
117	- **Never replace a registered connector operation with `core.logic.mock` because configuration cannot run** — if `registry search` / `registry get` finds `uipath.connector.<connector-key>.<operation>`, add that real connector node via `uip maestro flow node add`. Missing live connections, missing tenant access, or prompts that ask you to only plan `--detail` mean: run `node add`, write the planned `--detail` payload to a sidecar file (e.g. `<nodeId>.detail.json`), and surface "configure pending" as an Open Question. **Do not leave a partial `inputs.detail` on the node** — the validator rejects hand-authored envelopes, and the node will not pass `flow validate` until `node configure` is run. Studio Web and reviewers need the real connector key in the `.flow`; the agent must report this explicitly rather than letting the user discover it via a later validation failure. See [§ Node ownership](#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node) and [connector/impl.md — No-Live-Tenant / Planned Configuration](references/plugins/connector/impl.md#no-live-tenant--planned-configuration).
118	- **Never edit `content/*.bpmn`** — it is auto-generated from the `.flow` file and will be overwritten.
119	- **Never use `core.logic.mock` when the resource is in the same solution** — use `--local` discovery instead. Mock placeholders are only for resources that are not in the current solution and not yet published.
120	- **Never hand-write `definitions` entries** — always copy from registry output. Hand-written definitions have wrong port schemas and cause validation failures.
121	- **Never put any `model` block on node instances** — BPMN type, serviceType, event definition, binding templates, and context templates all live in the node's **definition** (copied verbatim from `registry get` into `definitions[]`). Instances carry only per-instance data: `inputs`, `outputs`, `display`. Identity fields like `entryPointId` / `isDefaultEntryPoint` (triggers) and `color` / `content` (sticky notes) live under `inputs`. This applies to every inline-agent-related node too: `uipath.agent.autonomous` plus every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) carries source identity at `inputs.source = <UUID>`. Their definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists onto the instance.
122	- **Never author `model.context[]` on resource-node instances** — resource-node instances have no `model` block. For `uipath.core.*` resource nodes (rpa, agent, flow, agentic-process, api-workflow, hitl), the definition (from `registry get`) already carries `model.context[]` with `<bindings.{name}>` placeholders. Your job is to add matching entries to the top-level `bindings[]` array — two entries per resource node (`name` + `folderPath`) with `resourceKey` matching the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey`. At BPMN emit, the runtime rewrites `<bindings.{name}>` → `=bindings.{id}` via `(resourceKey, name)` matching. Without the top-level `bindings[]` entries, `uip maestro flow validate` passes but `uip maestro flow debug` fails with "Folder does not exist or the user does not have access to the folder." See the resource plugin's `impl.md`.
123	- **Never put a `ui` block on node instances** — position and size belong in the top-level `layout.nodes` object. Nodes with `"ui": { "position": ... }` use the wrong format and may not render correctly in Studio Web.
124	- **Never skip `flow format` before publish or debug** — without it, hand-written `layout` data renders as misshapen rectangles in Studio Web (the MST-9061 failure mode). See rule #12 above for the format step.
125	- **Never validate after every individual edit** — intermediate flow states (e.g., node added but not yet wired) are expected to be invalid. Run `uip maestro flow validate` once after the full build is complete.
126	- **Never use `console.log` in script nodes** — `console` is not available in the Jint runtime. Use `return { debug: value }` to inspect values.
127	- **Never forget output mapping on End nodes** — every `out` variable in `variables.globals` must have a `source` expression in every reachable End node's `outputs`. Missing mappings cause silent runtime failures.
128	- **Never update `in` variables** — only `inout` variables can be modified via `variableUpdates`. Input variables are read-only after flow start.
129	- **Never reference parent-scope `$vars` inside a subflow** — subflows have isolated scope. Pass values explicitly via subflow inputs.
130	- **Never use `core.action.http` (v1)** — the v1 node is deprecated for all HTTP requests (both connector-authenticated and manual). For connector-auth, v1's `authenticationType: "connection"` input does not pass IS credentials at runtime. Use `core.action.http.v2` (Managed HTTP Request) for every HTTP node. See [http/planning.md](references/plugins/http/planning.md).
131	- **Never hand-write `definitions[]` or `inputs.*` for managed HTTP nodes** — use `uip maestro flow node add` (with `--input` for `branches` / `timeout` / `retryCount`) and `uip maestro flow node configure` (for `inputs.detail`). These are the only supported authoring paths. Hand-written `definitions[]` strips required manifest fields; hand-written `inputs.detail` misses `essentialConfiguration` and fails at runtime. See [http/impl.md](references/plugins/http/impl.md).
132	- **Never write `$vars.X` (or `$metadata.X`, `$self.X`) without `=js:` in value fields** — `flow validate` flags this as MST-9107. See rule #11 above and [shared/node-output-wiring.md](../shared/node-output-wiring.md) for the per-node-type field reference.
133	- **Never reuse a reference ID (mailbox folder, Slack channel, Jira project, Google Sheet, etc.) from a prior flow or session** — reference IDs are scoped to the specific authenticated account behind the connection. A `parentFolderId` from one Outlook mailbox is invalid in another; a Slack channel ID from one workspace is invalid in another. A reused ID passes `flow validate` and `node configure` cleanly, then faults silently at runtime with no resolvable error. Always re-resolve via `uip is resources run list <connector-key> <objectName> --connection-id <CURRENT_CONNECTION_ID> --output json` against the connection bound to this flow — do not paste a value you saw in another flow. See [connector/impl.md — Step 4](references/plugins/connector/impl.md) and [connector-trigger/impl.md — Step 3](references/plugins/connector-trigger/impl.md).
134	- **Never include `[*]` literally in a connector `bodyParameters` / `queryParameters` / `pathParameters` key** — `[*]` in `requestFields[].name` is an array marker, not part of the wire key. Strip it and pass an array value of the field's `dataType` (e.g. `"fields.labels[*]"` → `"fields.labels": ["a", "b"]`). Supported only when `[*]` is the name suffix; `[*].` (segments after) is not authorable. `flow validate` misses this; runtime rejects the key. See [connector/impl.md — Step 6b](references/plugins/connector/impl.md) for the full table including expression-value handling.

7	## Should you plan first?
8

12	- The flow has 5+ nodes with branching or parallel paths

14	- The user's requirements are ambiguous and you need to confirm the approach

16	**Don't plan when:**
17	- Adding/editing a single node in an existing flow (use [brownfield.md](brownfield.md))

22	
23	**Plan:** "Build a flow that receives a Jira ticket, classifies it with an AI agent, routes urgent tickets to Slack and non-urgent to a queue, and logs everything to a Google Sheet."

32	## Three-turn execution map
33	
34	Steps 0–6 are **logical phases**, not separate turns. A typical greenfield build collapses to **three assistant turns** (universal SKILL.md rule #10). Each step heading below carries a `[T1]` / `[T2]` / `[T3]` tag — emit every tool call inside the same Turn as one assistant message.
35	
36	| Turn | Steps | What you emit in ONE assistant message |
37	|---|---|---|
38	| **T1 — Setup + discovery** | 0, 1, 2, 3 | One chained `Bash` (scaffold + register + pull + `node add` for each CLI-owned node) **+** parallel `Bash` (one `registry get` per OOTB type you'll inline) **+** parallel `Read` (plugin `impl.md`s) **+** optional `uip login status`. **If existing `.uipx` solutions are present, the Step 2 gate fires first in its own turn** — resolve it before this chain. |
39	| **T2 — Read + author** | 4 | One `Read` of the `.flow` **+** a batch of `Edit` calls (or one `Write` if ≥70% of nodes change). Claude Code serializes Edits on the same file, so they don't race |
40	| **T3 — Finalize** | 5, 6 | One chained `Bash` (`node configure && validate && format`). On validate failure: one Edit turn, then re-chain `validate && format` |
41	
42	### Batching anti-patterns
43	
44	- **One CLI per turn.** Never issue `solution init`, then `cd`, then `flow init` as three separate Bash calls — chain with `&&`. Same for `node configure && validate && format`.
45	- **Sequential `registry get`s.** Emit every `registry get` as a parallel `Bash` in one message alongside the T1 scaffold chain.
46	- **Validating after every Edit.** Validate once at the end of T3 (or after a recovery Edit). Intermediate states are expected to be invalid.
47	- **Re-reading the `.flow` every turn.** `Read` once at the start of T2; subsequent `Edit`s in the same conversation don't need re-reading unless an external command (e.g., `node configure`, `format`) rewrites the file between Edits.
48	- **`Edit` in the same turn as a `Bash` that mutates the same file.** Parallel tool calls race — separate them across turns.
49	- **Two parallel `Edit`s anchored to the same byte range.** Same-file Edits serialize in execution order; if Edit N's `old_string` overlaps text that Edit N-1's substitution removed or shifted, Edit N fails with "string not found." Use the [per-array anchor pattern](#anchoring-parallel-flow-edits--anchor-on-what-you-read-not-on-key-order) — anchor each Edit on its target array's own opening key, never on key order or a shared boundary.

74	## Step 2 — Create a solution, THEN a Flow project inside it **[T1]**
75	
76	> **A Flow project cannot exist outside a solution** (universal rule in [SKILL.md](../../../SKILL.md)). Run `uip maestro flow init` (Step 2b) outside a solution and it now **auto-scaffolds** one — `<Project>Solution/<Project>Solution.uipx` with the project nested at `<Project>Solution/<Project>/` (response carries `Data.AutoCreatedSolution`). Still scaffold or select the solution first (Step 2a) so the solution name matches the project name rather than the auto `<Project>Solution`, and so discovery is unambiguous. The correct layout is **always** `<Solution>/<Project>/<Project>.flow` (double-nested — see the tree after Step 2c). Passing `--skip-solution-registration` opts out of both auto-scaffold and registration, leaving a bare single-nested layout that fails Studio Web upload and packaging.

78	Check for existing solutions with `ls *.uipx */*.uipx 2>/dev/null` (each solution is its own folder — `<Solution>/<Solution>.uipx` — so a bare `*.uipx` misses them). If any are found, **STOP before the T1 chain — do not run `uip solution init` yet** — and ask via `AskUserQuestion`, presenting a dropdown with one option per discovered `.uipx`, a **"Create a new solution"** option, and **"Something else"** as the last option. See the dropdown question rule in [SKILL.md](../../../SKILL.md).

83	### Canonical T1 chain — issue this as ONE `Bash` call
84	
85	This is the consolidated command that does Steps 2a + 2b + Step 3 + (optionally) one `node add` per CLI-owned node, in one chained Bash. `node add` signature is `<file> <node-type>` (file first):
86	
87	```bash
88	uip solution init "<SolutionName>" --output json \
89	  && cd "<SolutionName>" \
90	  && uip maestro flow init "<ProjectName>" --output json \
91	  && cd "<ProjectName>" \
92	  && uip maestro flow registry pull \
93	  && uip maestro flow node add "<ProjectName>.flow" core.action.http.v2 --label "<NodeLabel>" --output json
94	```
95	
96	Tail-append one `node add` per CLI-owned node (`uipath.connector.*`, `uipath.connector.trigger.*`, `core.action.http.v2`). Each `node add` returns the new node `id` in `Data` — capture it from the chained output for T2/T3. Drop the trailing `node add` segment when the flow is OOTB-only.
97	
98	In the SAME assistant message (parallel to this chain): emit one `Bash` per OOTB `registry get <NODE_TYPE>` you'll need in T2 (always `core.control.end` — see Step 4), and parallel `Read` calls for any plugin `impl.md`s you'll consult.
99	
100	> **Older `solution-tool` (< 1.0.0)** used `solution new` (see [.claude/rules/cli-renames.md](../../../../../.claude/rules/cli-renames.md)). If `solution init` returns `unknown command`, substitute `solution new`.

104	### 2a. Create a new solution
105	
106	```bash
107	uip solution init "<SolutionName>" --output json
108	```
109	
110	Creates `<cwd>/<SolutionName>/<SolutionName>.uipx`. **`cd` into the new solution directory before Step 2b.**
111	
112	> **Naming convention:** Use the same name for both the solution and the project unless the user specifies otherwise. If the user only provides a project name, use it as the solution name too.
113	
114	### 2b. Create the Flow project inside the solution folder
115	
116	```bash
117	cd <directory>/<SolutionName> && uip maestro flow init <ProjectName> --output json
118	```
119	
120	The `cd` puts the project inside the solution you just created. Skip it and `flow init` won't find that solution (discovery walks **up**, not down into `<SolutionName>/`) — it auto-scaffolds a **second, separate** `<ProjectName>Solution/` beside your empty `<SolutionName>/`, leaving two solutions. The project no longer single-nests, but `cd` first to land in the right one.
121	
122	> **Bash session state persists across tool calls.** This `cd` is **not scoped to one Bash invocation** — your cwd remains inside `<SolutionName>/` for every subsequent `Bash` call until you `cd` somewhere else. Plan the rest of Step 2 (and Steps 3–6) accordingly: either keep using paths relative to the solution dir, or anchor with `$(pwd)` / the absolute `Data.Path` returned by `flow init`. Do NOT prefix later commands with the original `<directory>/<SolutionName>/...` — that would resolve as `<SolutionName>/<directory>/<SolutionName>/...` and look like a layout bug when it isn't.
123	
124	`--output json` is required so Step 2c can inspect `Data.SolutionRegistration.Status` to confirm the project was auto-registered with the parent solution.

126	### 2c. Verify the project is registered in the solution
127	
128	When `uip maestro flow init` is run from inside a solution directory (Step 2b), it **auto-registers** the project with the nearest parent `.uipx`. Run outside any solution, it **auto-scaffolds** `<Project>Solution/` and registers the project in it — the response then also carries `Data.AutoCreatedSolution` (`{ Name, Path, SolutionFile }`) and `Status: Registered`. Pass `--skip-solution-registration` to opt out of both (Status `OptedOut`, bare single-nested layout). The success envelope always reports the outcome in `Data.SolutionRegistration`:
129	
130	```json
131	{
132	  "Result": "Success",
133	  "Code": "FlowInit",
134	  "Data": {
135	    "Status": "Created successfully",
136	    "Path": ".../<SolutionName>/<ProjectName>",
137	    "SolutionRegistration": {
138	      "Status": "Registered",                     // or "AlreadyRegistered"
139	      "Solution": ".../<SolutionName>.uipx",
140	      "Project": "<ProjectName>/project.uiproj",
141	      "ProjectId": "<uuid>"
142	    }
143	  }
144	}
145	```
146	
147	If `Data.SolutionRegistration.Status` is `Registered` or `AlreadyRegistered`, **you are done** with this step — proceed to the layout check. If it is `OptedOut`, you passed `--skip-solution-registration` and the skip was intentional.
148	
149	**Fallback** — when `Status` is `Skipped` (ambiguous discovery — e.g. multiple `.uipx`), `Failed` (the `.uipx` write failed), or `NotInSolution` (rare — auto-scaffold did not run and no parent `.uipx` was found): wire the project manually.
150	
151	```bash
152	uip solution project add \
153	  <directory>/<SolutionName>/<ProjectName> \
154	  <directory>/<SolutionName>/<SolutionName>.uipx
155	```
156	
157	If you ended up with a bare single-nested layout (e.g. `--skip-solution-registration` was passed), **delete the partial scaffold and restart from Step 2a** — do not try to patch the layout by hand. See [diagnose/references/failure-modes.md — Single-nested layout](../../diagnose/references/failure-modes.md#single-nested-layout).

233	## Step 4 — Build the flow **[T2]**
234	
235	> **`flow init` scaffolds ONLY the manual trigger (`start` / `core.trigger.manual`) with zero edges.** Every other user-owned node — **including the End node** — is yours to add via `Edit` / `Write`. Any HTTP / connector / connector-trigger node you `node add`-ed in T1 is already in `nodes[]` and `definitions[]` but has empty `inputs.detail` (filled in T3) and is not wired yet.
236	
237	### T2 batch — issue these in ONE assistant message
238	
239	1. **One `Read`** of `<ProjectName>.flow` — required before any Edit/Write; T1's chained Bash mutated the file and Claude Code's file-state tracker does not auto-refresh on external mutations.
240	2. **A batch of parallel `Edit` calls** — one per top-level array you're modifying. Same-file Edits serialize in execution order, so each `old_string` must anchor to text NO OTHER parallel Edit modifies. Use the **per-array anchor pattern** below.
241	   - Edit `nodes[]` — add the End node (and any other user-owned nodes).
242	   - Edit `definitions[]` — paste the End definition verbatim from T1's `registry get core.control.end` output.
243	   - Edit `edges[]` — wire `trigger → <httpNode> → end`. End-node `outputs` mapping goes here too if you declared an `out` variable in `variables.globals`.
244	   - Edit `layout.nodes` — placeholder `{ position: { x: 0, y: 0 }, size: { width: 96, height: 96 }, collapsed: false }` per new node; `format` rewrites both position and size (by node shape) in T3.
245	
246	   `Write` of the whole file is allowed but token-costly on flows >~10 nodes — only fall back to `Write` when ≥70% of nodes change AND the file is small (see [editing-operations.md — Tool Selection Ladder](editing-operations.md#tool-selection-ladder)).
247	
248	#### Anchoring parallel `.flow` Edits — anchor on what you Read, not on key order
249	
250	> **Do not assume a top-level key order.** The CLI does not guarantee which keys are present or in what sequence — fixtures show `runtime` before `nodes` on one flow and absent on another, and `bindings` / `variables` / `solutionId` / `projectId` / `metadata` appear in varying positions. Any anchor of the form "closing `]` + the NEXT top-level key" is coupled to that ordering and will silently break across CLI versions or between flows. **Anchor on the target array's OWN key instead — you just `Read` the file at the top of T2, so anchor to text that read actually contains.**
251	
252	Anchor each Edit using its target array's own opening key, located in the text you just Read — not adjacency to a neighbor key. The catch: `"nodes": [` and `"edges": [` are NOT unique in the file. They recur **inside inline `definitions[]`** (an HTTP v2 / agent / subprocess definition embeds its own nested `nodes`/`edges`) **and inside any `subflows.<id>` block** (each subflow holds its own `nodes`/`edges`) — so even a small flow can carry several copies. The reliable, version-independent discriminator is **indentation: the top-level array sits at 2-space indent; every nested one is deeper.** `"definitions": [` and the top-level `"layout": {` appear once each, so they need no disambiguation.
253	
254	| Edit target | Anchor on (from the text you Read) | How to insert |
255	|---|---|---|
256	| Append to `nodes[]` | The **2-space-indented** `\n  "nodes": [` (the top-level array — deeper-indented `"nodes": ["` inside definitions do not match the two-leading-space prefix) plus the `start` node's opening `{ "id": "start"`. | Insert the new node object as the first element, immediately after the `[`: `\n    { new node JSON },`. Head-insertion keeps `old_string` clear of the array's closing `]`. |
257	| Append to `edges[]` | The **2-space-indented** `\n  "edges": [`. Empty after `flow init` (`\n  "edges": []`); the 2-space prefix distinguishes it from nested `edges` arrays. | When empty, replace `\n  "edges": []` with `\n  "edges": [\n    { new edge JSON }\n  ]`. When non-empty, anchor through the first edge and insert the new edge as the first element. |
258	| Append to `definitions[]` | `"definitions": [` plus the first definition's opening bytes. Top-level `definitions[]` is the only one in the file, so this is reliably unique. | Insert the new definition right after the opening `[`, as the first element. Never anchor on whatever key follows `definitions` — that key varies (`runtime`, `bindings`, `variables`, `layout`, depending on CLI version and what the flow contains). |
259	| Add an entry to `layout.nodes` | `"layout": {\n    "nodes": {\n      "start":` — `start` is the always-present trigger and the first key under `layout.nodes` in `init`-scaffolded flows. The top-level `"layout": {` is the only one. | `"layout":` + `"start":` jointly disambiguate. Insert `"<newId>": { ... },\n      ` before `"start":`. CLI-owned nodes added via `node add` already have a `layout.nodes` entry — only add entries for nodes you author by hand (e.g. End). |
260	
261	**Why head-insertion.** Inserting the new element right after the array's opening `[` means the `old_string` never includes the array's closing `]` — so it cannot collide with a closing `]` from a nested object (`form.sections[].fields[]`), and it never references a sibling top-level key whose position is not guaranteed. JSON array element order is not semantically significant for `nodes` / `edges` / `definitions`, so head vs. tail insertion is equivalent; `flow format` normalizes layout regardless.
262	
263	**Disjointness rule.** Two parallel Edits MUST anchor on DIFFERENT top-level arrays — nodes-Edit on the top-level `nodes[]`, edges-Edit on the top-level `edges[]`, definitions-Edit on `definitions[]`, layout-Edit on `layout.nodes`. Because each anchors on its own array (not a shared boundary), the parallel Edits never overlap — provided each anchor is unique first (see below).
264	
265	**Pre-flight uniqueness check.** Before submitting an Edit, confirm your `old_string` appears **exactly once** in the file you Read. `"definitions": [` and the top-level `"layout": {` are reliably unique. `"nodes": [` and `"edges": [` are NOT — they recur inside inline definitions and subflows, so anchor on the **2-space-indented** occurrence and extend through the first element's opening (e.g. `"id": "start"`) until the match count is one. Never anchor on a bare bracket shape, and never assume the first textual occurrence is the top-level one.
266	
267	**Safer fallback when in doubt:** serialize the Edits across two turns. One extra turn is cheaper than a failed-Edit recovery loop (which forces a re-Read, a re-derived anchor, and a re-submit).
268	
269	See [shared/file-format.md — Top-level structure](../../shared/file-format.md#top-level-structure) for which top-level keys exist and the note that their order is not guaranteed.
270	
271	> **Intra-turn ordering.** If a parallel `Edit` fails with "file not read," split `Read` into its own turn (cost: +1 turn).

293	  && uip maestro flow validate "<ProjectName>.flow" --output json \
294	  && uip maestro flow format "<ProjectName>.flow" --output json

297	`<DETAIL_JSON>` is node-type-specific — the schema is owned by each CLI-owned node's plugin, not duplicated here: HTTP → [http/impl.md](plugins/http/impl.md#critical-use-node-configure), connectors → [connector/impl.md](plugins/connector/impl.md), connector triggers → [connector-trigger/impl.md](plugins/connector-trigger/impl.md). 68	    "retryCount": 3,
69	    "branches": [
70	      { "id": "hasItems", "name": "Has Items", "conditionExpression": "$self.output.body.items.length > 0" },

82	### Dynamic values in URL / headers / body / query
83	
84	**IS activity input fields do not resolve `{$vars.x}` brace-templates.** The flow runtime's `{...}` template interpolation only applies to native flow fields (end-node output `source`, variable updates, decision `expression`, script body, etc.) — **not** to fields under `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` on HTTP v2 or on any `uipath.connector.*` activity. Evidence: `"url": "https://.../user/{$vars.article}/..."` ships to the service as literal `{vars.article}` (the `$` is stripped, braces remain), producing a 400 Bad Request.
85	
86	**Use `=js:` expressions for any dynamic value in IS activity inputs.** The runtime evaluates `=js:` before handing the value to the connector:
87	
88	```json
89	"bodyParameters": {
90	  "url": "=js:`https://api.example.com/users/${$vars.userId}/orders`",
91	  "headers": {
92	    "Authorization": "=js:'Bearer ' + $vars.apiToken",
93	    "X-Request-ID": "=js:$metadata.instanceId"
94	  },
95	  "query": {
96	    "since": "=js:$vars.startDate"
97	  }
98	}
99	```
100	
101	Template literals with `${...}` interpolation work because the whole expression is evaluated as JavaScript — `$vars` is a global in the `=js:` context. Plain string concatenation (`'Bearer ' + $vars.token`) works the same way.
102	
103	When calling `uip maestro flow node configure --detail`, pass the `=js:` string verbatim — the CLI stores it in `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` unchanged:

105	```bash
106	uip maestro flow node configure <Project>.flow <nodeId> \
107	  --detail '{
108	    "authentication": "manual",
109	    "method": "GET",
110	    "url": "=js:`https://api.example.com/users/${$vars.userId}`"
111	  }' --output json
112	```

116	Skip this section unless you need to route downstream paths based on the *response content* (e.g., `items.length > 0` vs empty). Do **not** use `branches` just to handle call failures — for that, use the `error` port (see [Wire edges](#wire-edges)).

135	### Wire edges
136	
137	The managed HTTP node's target port is `input`. Its source ports are:
138	
139	- `default` — primary success output (or fallback when configured branches don't match)
140	- `error` — fires when the HTTP call fails (network error, timeout, non-2xx not caught by a branch); wire this to an error handler to keep the flow from faulting
141	- `branch-{id}` — one per entry in `inputs.branches` ([Conditional branches](#conditional-branches)); use the exact `id` you set

147	  "id": "e-<upstreamNodeId>-<nodeId>",
148	  "sourceNodeId": "<upstreamNodeId>",
149	  "sourcePort": "<port>",
150	  "targetNodeId": "<nodeId>",
151	  "targetPort": "input"
152	}
153	```
154	
155	```json

157	  "id": "e-<nodeId>-<downstreamNodeId>",
158	  "sourceNodeId": "<nodeId>",
159	  "sourcePort": "default",
160	  "targetNodeId": "<downstreamNodeId>",
161	  "targetPort": "input"

169	  "sourcePort": "error",
170	  "targetNodeId": "<errorHandlerId>",
171	  "targetPort": "input"

175	When an HTTP node has an outgoing `error` edge, the HTTP node instance must also include `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true`. `uip maestro flow edge add --source-port error` and `uip maestro flow format` set this automatically; direct JSON edits must set it explicitly.

177	```json

179	  "id": "e-<nodeId>-<hasItemsDownstream>",

189	| Error | Cause | Fix |
190	| --- | --- | --- |
191	| `not_authed` or 401/403 | Wrong node type (v1 instead of v2), missing bindings, or expired connection | Verify node type is `core.action.http.v2`, check `bindings_v2.json` exists, ping the connection |
192	| `configuration` field missing | Node not configured via CLI | Run `uip maestro flow node configure` — do not hand-write `inputs.detail` |
193	| `flow validate` errors with `uiPathActivityTypeId` missing on `core.action.http.v2` | Node was hand-authored in `definitions[]` instead of via `uip maestro flow node add` | Remove the node, re-add it via `uip maestro flow node add <file> core.action.http.v2 ...`, then re-run `node configure`. |
194	| Connection not found | Wrong connection ID or connector key | Re-run `uip is connections list` for the target connector |
195	| Wrong API response | Incorrect `url` or `query` | Check the target service's API documentation |
196	| `ImplicitConnection` errors | Manual mode misconfigured | Verify `authentication: "manual"` and `url` is a full URL |
197	| Flow faults on 4xx/5xx response | No `error` edge wired from the HTTP node | Add an edge with `sourcePort: "error"` to an error-handler node. See [Implicit error port on action nodes](../../../../shared/file-format.md#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes) — same mechanism applies to all action nodes |
198	| Edge `source-port output` rejected | Referencing the variable namespace as a port name | HTTP source ports are `default`, `error`, and `branch-{id}` — not `output`. The `output` name is only a variable namespace (`$vars.{nodeId}.output`) |

1	# Transform Node — Implementation
2	
3	## Node Types
4	
5	- `core.action.transform` — generic (chains multiple operations)
6	- `core.action.transform.filter` — filter only
7	- `core.action.transform.map` — map only
8	- `core.action.transform.group-by` — group-by only
9	
10	## Registry Validation
11	
12	```bash
13	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.transform --output json
14	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.transform.filter --output json
15	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.transform.map --output json
16	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.transform.group-by --output json
17	```
18	
19	Confirm: input port `input`, output ports `output` and `error`, required inputs `collection` and `operations`. Set each node instance's `typeVersion` to the `version` field from the matching response — do not hardcode it.
20	
21	## Adding / Editing
22	
23	For step-by-step add, delete, and wiring procedures, see [editing-operations.md](../../editing-operations.md). Use the JSON structures below for the node-specific `inputs` and `model` fields.
24	
25	## Collection Input Contract
26	
27	`inputs.collection` is a transform-specific path field, not a general `=js:` value field. Set it to the variable path that contains the array:
28	
29	```json
30	"collection": "$vars.orders.output.items"
31	```
32	
33	**NEVER** wrap transform `collection` in `=js:`. **NEVER** set it to an inline array literal. Both forms below are wrong:
34	
35	```json
36	"collection": "=js:$vars.orders.output.items"
37	```
38	
39	```json
40	"collection": "=js:[{\"title\":\"Example\"}]"
41	```
42	
43	The transform runtime turns the path string into a lookup such as `vars.orders.output.items`. If the string starts with `=js:` or contains an inline JSON/JS literal, that lookup resolves to an empty collection.
44	
45	For static data, store the array in a workflow variable `defaultValue` or emit it from an upstream static-data/script node, then point `collection` at that variable or node output. Filtering, mapping, and grouping still belong in transform nodes.
46	
47	---
48	
49	## Generic Transform (`core.action.transform`)
50	
51	Chains multiple operations (filter -> map -> groupBy) in a single node. Operations execute in order; each feeds into the next.
52	
53	```json
54	{
55	  "id": "transformChain",
56	  "type": "core.action.transform",
57	  "typeVersion": "<DEFINITION_VERSION>",
58	  "display": { "label": "Process Employees" },
59	  "inputs": {
60	    "collection": "$vars.fetchData.output.body.employees",
61	    "operations": [
62	      {
63	        "id": "op1",
64	        "type": "filter",
65	        "config": {
66	          "operation": "and",
67	          "filters": [
68	            { "id": "f1", "field": "active", "condition": "equals", "value": true }
69	          ]
70	        }
71	      },
72	      {
73	        "id": "op2",
74	        "type": "map",
75	        "config": {
76	          "keepOriginalFields": false,
77	          "mappings": [
78	            { "id": "m1", "field": "name", "transformation": "uppercase", "renameTo": "fullName" },
79	            { "id": "m2", "field": "salary", "transformation": "copy", "renameTo": "" }
80	          ]
81	        }
82	      }
83	    ]
84	  },
85	  "outputs": {
86	    "output": {
87	      "type": "object",
88	      "description": "The return value of the transform",
89	      "source": "=result.response",
90	      "var": "output"
91	    },
92	    "error": {
93	      "type": "object",
94	      "description": "Error information if the transform fails",
95	      "source": "=Error",
96	      "var": "error"
97	    }
98	  }
99	}
100	```
101	
102	---
103	
104	## Filter (`core.action.transform.filter`)
105	
106	```json
107	{
108	  "id": "filterActive",
109	  "type": "core.action.transform.filter",
110	  "typeVersion": "<DEFINITION_VERSION>",
111	  "display": { "label": "Filter Active Orders" },
112	  "inputs": {
113	    "collection": "$vars.orders.output.items",
114	    "operations": [
115	      {
116	        "id": "op1",
117	        "type": "filter",
118	        "config": {
119	          "operation": "and",
120	          "filters": [
121	            { "id": "f1", "field": "status", "condition": "equals", "value": "active" },
122	            { "id": "f2", "field": "amount", "condition": "greater_equal", "value": 100 }
123	          ]
124	        }
125	      }
126	    ]
127	  },
128	  "outputs": {
129	    "output": {
130	      "type": "object",
131	      "description": "The return value of the transform",
132	      "source": "=result.response",
133	      "var": "output"
134	    },
135	    "error": {
136	      "type": "object",
137	      "description": "Error information if the transform fails",
138	      "source": "=Error",
139	      "var": "error"
140	    }
141	  }
142	}
143	```
144	
145	**Filter conditions:** `equals`, `not_equals`, `greater_than`, `less_than`, `greater_equal`, `less_equal`, `contains`, `starts_with`, `ends_with`, `is_null`, `is_not_null`
146	
147	**Filter operations:** `and` (all conditions must match), `or` (any condition matches)
148	
149	> **Filter `value` is literal-only — no `$vars`, no `=js:`, no brace-templates.** The Transform runtime reads `value` as-is and does not evaluate expressions. Setting `"value": "$vars.threshold"`, `"value": "=js:$vars.threshold"`, or `"value": "{$vars.threshold}"` silently produces an empty filtered array — the filter is comparing each item's field against the literal string `$vars.threshold` (or `=js:...`), never against the intended number. Only literal scalars work: `"value": 500`, `"value": "active"`, `"value": true`. If you need a dynamic threshold, compute the filter inside a [Script](../script/impl.md) node instead, or hoist the literal into the flow design and keep the Transform filter for demo-time thresholds.
150	
151	**`field` accepts dot-paths** for nested object fields (e.g., `"field": "order.amount"`). Applies to `collection` elements.
152	
153	---
154	
155	## Map (`core.action.transform.map`)
156	
157	```json
158	{
159	  "id": "mapFields",
160	  "type": "core.action.transform.map",
161	  "typeVersion": "<DEFINITION_VERSION>",
162	  "display": { "label": "Normalize Names" },
163	  "inputs": {
164	    "collection": "$vars.rawData.output.items",
165	    "operations": [
166	      {
167	        "id": "op1",
168	        "type": "map",
169	        "config": {
170	          "keepOriginalFields": false,
171	          "mappings": [
172	            { "id": "m1", "field": "firstName", "transformation": "uppercase", "renameTo": "name" },
173	            { "id": "m2", "field": "email", "transformation": "lowercase", "renameTo": "" },
174	            { "id": "m3", "field": "dept", "transformation": "copy", "renameTo": "department" }
175	          ]
176	        }
177	      }
178	    ]
179	  },
180	  "outputs": {
181	    "output": {
182	      "type": "object",
183	      "description": "The return value of the transform",
184	      "source": "=result.response",
185	      "var": "output"
186	    },
187	    "error": {
188	      "type": "object",
189	      "description": "Error information if the transform fails",
190	      "source": "=Error",
191	      "var": "error"
192	    }
193	  }
194	}
195	```
196	
197	**Transformations:** `copy` (no change), `uppercase`, `lowercase`, `trim` (remove leading/trailing whitespace).
198	
199	**`keepOriginalFields`:** When `false`, only mapped fields appear in output. When `true`, unmapped fields pass through.
200	
201	**`renameTo`:** New field name. Empty string (`""`) keeps the original name.
202	
203	---
204	
205	## Group By (`core.action.transform.group-by`)
206	
207	```json
208	{
209	  "id": "groupByDept",
210	  "type": "core.action.transform.group-by",
211	  "typeVersion": "<DEFINITION_VERSION>",
212	  "display": { "label": "Group by Department" },
213	  "inputs": {
214	    "collection": "$vars.employees.output.items",
215	    "operations": [
216	      {
217	        "id": "op1",
218	        "type": "groupBy",
219	        "config": {
220	          "groupByField": "department",
221	          "aggregations": [
222	            { "id": "a1", "field": "", "operation": "count", "alias": "headcount" },
223	            { "id": "a2", "field": "salary", "operation": "sum", "alias": "totalSalary" },
224	            { "id": "a3", "field": "salary", "operation": "average", "alias": "avgSalary" },
225	            { "id": "a4", "field": "salary", "operation": "min", "alias": "minSalary" },
226	            { "id": "a5", "field": "salary", "operation": "max", "alias": "maxSalary" },
227	            { "id": "a6", "field": "name", "operation": "collect", "alias": "names" },
228	            { "id": "a7", "field": "name", "operation": "first", "alias": "firstHire" }
229	          ]
230	        }
231	      }
232	    ]
233	  },
234	  "outputs": {
235	    "output": {
236	      "type": "object",
237	      "description": "The return value of the transform",
238	      "source": "=result.response",
239	      "var": "output"
240	    },
241	    "error": {
242	      "type": "object",
243	      "description": "Error information if the transform fails",
244	      "source": "=Error",
245	      "var": "error"
246	    }
247	  }
248	}
249	```
250	
251	**Aggregation operations:**
252	
253	| Operation | Description | `field` required |
254	| --- | --- | --- |
255	| `count` | Number of items in group | No |
256	| `sum` | Sum of numeric field | Yes |
257	| `average` | Average of numeric field | Yes |
258	| `min` | Minimum value | Yes |
259	| `max` | Maximum value | Yes |
260	| `collect` | Array of all field values | Yes |
261	| `first` | First item's field value | Yes |
262	| `last` | Last item's field value | Yes |
263

265	
266	## Debug
267	
268	| Error | Cause | Fix |
269	| --- | --- | --- |
270	| Filter passes all items through | Wrong condition name (e.g. `greater` instead of `greater_than`) | Use exact names: `equals`, `not_equals`, `greater_than`, `less_than`, `greater_equal`, `less_equal`, `contains`, `starts_with`, `ends_with`, `is_null`, `is_not_null` |
271	| Filter silently returns empty array | Filter `value` holds an unresolved expression (`"$vars.x"`, `"=js:..."`, `"{$vars.x}"`) — Transform compares each item against that string literal | Replace with a literal scalar (`"value": 500`); expressions are not evaluated in filter `value`. If the threshold must be dynamic, do the filter in a Script node |
272	| Collection is null/empty | `collection` was wrapped in `=js:` or set to an inline array literal instead of a plain variable path | Use a path such as `"$vars.loadCatalog.output.catalog"` or `"$vars.catalog"`; keep static arrays in a variable default or upstream node |
273	| Map output missing fields | `keepOriginalFields: false` and field not in mappings | Add the field to mappings or set `keepOriginalFields: true` |
274	| GroupBy produces empty groups | No items match the group field | Check `groupByField` matches actual field names in the data |

1	# HTTP Request Node — Manual Mode
2	
3	Use this walkthrough when there is no IS connector for the target service, the API needs no auth (or auth you pass yourself in headers), or you are prototyping against an arbitrary REST endpoint. For connector-managed auth, use [impl-connector.md](impl-connector.md) instead.
4	
5	**No connection lookup required.** Manual mode uses `ImplicitConnection` — there are no IS bindings.
6	
7	Before starting, read [impl.md](impl.md) for the node type, registry validation, and the "always use `node configure`" rule. Follow Steps 1–4 in order.
8	
9	## Step 1 — Add the node
10	
11	```bash
12	uip maestro flow node add <ProjectName>.flow core.action.http.v2 \
13	  --label "<HTTP node label>" --output json
14	```
15	
16	The CLI copies the manifest into `definitions[]`, adds the node instance, registers `variables.nodes`, and inserts a `layout.nodes` placeholder — byte-for-byte from the registry. Save the returned `<nodeId>` — Step 2 reuses it. Leave `inputs` empty; Step 2 populates `inputs.detail`. Do not hand-author the definition — see [impl.md — Add the node](impl.md#add-the-node).
17	
18	## Step 2 — Configure the node
19	
20	> **Find missing values first.** Before composing `url` / `query` / `body`, resolve any values the agent doesn't have (IDs from names, required body fields, response shape, …). See [/uipath:uipath-platform — http-request.md](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/http-request.md).
21	
22	```bash
23	uip maestro flow node configure <ProjectName>.flow <nodeId> \
24	  --detail '{
25	    "authentication": "manual",
26	    "method": "GET",
27	    "url": "https://api.example.com/endpoint",
28	    "query": {"param1": "value1"}
29	  }' --output json
30	```
31	
32	The CLI:
33	
34	- Builds the full `inputs.detail` (manual auth, `ImplicitConnection`, bodyParameters, essentialConfiguration)
35	- Does **not** generate `bindings_v2.json` or a connection resource file — manual mode needs neither
36	
37	`url` must be a full URL (scheme + host + path). For auth headers you control, pass them under `headers`:
38	
39	```bash
40	uip maestro flow node configure <ProjectName>.flow <nodeId> \
41	  --detail '{
42	    "authentication": "manual",
43	    "method": "GET",
44	    "url": "https://api.example.com/me",
45	    "headers": {"Authorization": "=js:`Bearer ${$vars.apiToken}`"}
46	  }' --output json
47	```
48	
49	**Dynamic values:** HTTP input fields do not resolve `{$vars.x}` brace-templates — use `=js:` expressions for any dynamic `url` / `headers` / `body` / `query`. Pass the `=js:` string verbatim in `--detail`. Full rationale and examples: [impl.md — Dynamic values](impl.md#dynamic-values-in-url--headers--body--query).
50	
51	## Step 3 — (Optional) Response branches
52	
53	Skip unless you need to route downstream paths based on response content (e.g., `items.length > 0` vs empty). For generic call-failure handling use the `error` port in Step 4 instead. Full syntax and rules: [impl.md — Conditional branches](impl.md#conditional-branches).
54	
55	## Step 4 — Wire edges
56	
57	The HTTP node's target port is `input`. Source ports: `default` (success), `error` (network/non-2xx), `branch-{id}` (one per Step 3 entry). Wire `default` to the next node and `error` to a handler — without an `error` edge, a failed call faults the flow.
58	
59	Edge JSON shapes and all four examples (upstream→node, default→downstream, error→handler, branch→downstream): [impl.md — Wire edges](impl.md#wire-edges).
60	
61	## Debug
62	
63	See [impl.md — Debug](impl.md#debug). For manual mode, watch for `ImplicitConnection` errors — they signal a missing `authentication: "manual"` flag or a non-URL `url` value.
64

1	# Script Node — Implementation
2	
3	## Node Type
4	
5	`core.action.script`
6	
7	## Registry validation
8	
9	```bash
10	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.script --output json
11	```
12	
13	Confirm: input port `input`, output port `success`, required input `script` (string, non-empty). See [Action Node Structure — Registry validation](../../../../shared/action-nodes.md#registry-validation) for the shared pattern.
14	
15	## JSON structure
16	
17	Follow the [Action Node Structure — Standard JSON skeleton](../../../../shared/action-nodes.md#standard-json-skeleton). The script-specific input is a single `script` string:
18	
19	```json
20	{
21	  "inputs": {
22	    "script": "const items = $vars.fetchData.output.body.items;\nconst total = items.reduce((sum, i) => sum + i.amount, 0);\nreturn { total, count: items.length };"
23	  }
24	}
25	```
26	
27	## Adding and editing
28	
29	See [Action Node Structure — Adding and editing procedures](../../../../shared/action-nodes.md#adding-and-editing-procedures). The script node uses the standard input port `input` and output port `success`; no plugin-specific wiring.
30	
31	## Script rules
32	
33	1. **Top-level body — no `function main()` wrapper.** Node runs the `script` text directly (as a function body); a wrapper is never called → `output` null. Read workflow variables via `$vars.<variableId>` and upstream node outputs via `$vars.<nodeId>.output`; end with top-level `return {…}`. Not a coded Function: no `main`, no injected args.
34	   - Correct: `const n = $vars.ixp1.output.field; return { n };`
35	   - Wrong: `function main({ ixp1 }) { … }`
36	2. **Must `return` an object** — `return { key: value }`, not a bare scalar. The return value becomes `$vars.<nodeId>.output`.
37	3. **`$vars` is a global** — use it directly: `return { upper: $vars.customerName.toUpperCase() }`
38	4. **JavaScript ES2020 (Jint engine)** — see [variables-and-expressions.md](../../../../shared/variables-and-expressions.md) for supported features and Jint constraints.
39	5. **No `console.log`** — `console` is not available. Use `return { debug: value }` to inspect values.
40	6. **No external calls** — use the HTTP node or a connector node for API calls.
41	7. **30-second timeout** — long-running computations will be killed.
42	
43	## Common patterns
44	
45	### Transform and return
46	
47	```javascript
48	const items = $vars.fetchData.output.body.items;
49	const filtered = items.filter(i => i.status === "active");
50	return { items: filtered, count: filtered.length };
51	```
52	
53	### Build a payload for a downstream node
54	
55	```javascript
56	return {
57	  subject: `Order ${$vars.orderId} - Confirmation`,
58	  body: `Your order of ${$vars.orderTotal} has been processed.`,
59	  recipient: $vars.customerEmail
60	};
61	```
62	
63	### Error check from upstream
64	
65	```javascript
66	const error = $vars.httpCall.error;
67	if (error) {
68	  return { hasError: true, message: error.message };
69	}
70	return { hasError: false, data: $vars.httpCall.output.body };
71	```
72	
73	### Reading a file-typed variable
74	
75	A `file` variable (bound via `uip maestro flow debug --attachment <id>=<path>`) hydrates as an **object**, not a string. Read the uploaded file's name from `.FullName`:
76	
77	```javascript
78	const doc = $vars.start.output.inputDoc; // file variable → object
79	return { fileName: doc.FullName };        // .FullName, not .name/.fileName
80	```
81	
82	Property access is **case-sensitive** — these casings resolve: `.FullName`, `.ID` (uppercase, not `.Id`), `.MimeType`, `.Metadata.size` (nested, lowercase `size`). `.name` / `.fileName` do not exist. See [variables-and-expressions.md — Runtime shape of a `file` variable](../../../../shared/variables-and-expressions.md#file-input).
83	
84	## Debug
85	
86	| Error | Cause | Fix |
87	| --- | --- | --- |
88	| Script did not return a value | Missing `return` statement | Add `return { ... }` |
89	| `output` is `null` but script has a `return` | `return` is inside an uncalled `function main(){}` wrapper | Remove wrapper; code + `return` at top level (rule 1) |
90	| Return value is not an object | Returned a scalar (`return 42`) | Wrap in object: `return { value: 42 }` |
91	| `$vars.nodeId` is undefined | Upstream node not connected or wrong ID | Check edges and node IDs |
92	| Timeout after 30s | Script too expensive | Simplify logic or split into multiple scripts |
93	| `console is not defined` | Used `console.log()` | Remove — use `return { debug: val }` instead |
94	| `fetch is not defined` | Tried to make HTTP call | Use an HTTP node or connector node instead |

It contains three sections: 38 39 ```json 40 { 41 "variables": { 42 "globals": [], 43 "nodes": [], 44 "variableUpdates": {} 45 } 46 } 47 ``` 48 49 | Section | Purpose | 50 | --- | --- | 51 | `globals` | Workflow-level variables: inputs, outputs, and state | 52 | `nodes` | Node output variables (auto-generated when using CLI `node add`) | 53 | `variableUpdates` | Per-node expressions that update state variables | 54 55 --- 56 57 ## Workflow Variables (`globals`) 58 59 Workflow variables are declared in `variables.globals`. Each has a **direction** that determines its role. 60 61 ### Directions 62 63 | Direction | Role | Readable | Writable | Use case | 64 | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | 65 | `in` | External input | Yes | No | Values passed when the flow is triggered or called | 66 | `out` | Workflow output | Yes | Mapped on End node | Values returned when the flow completes | 67 | `inout` | Internal state | Yes | Yes (via `variableUpdates`) | Counters, accumulators, flags shared across nodes | 68 69 ### Schema 70 71 ```typescript 72 { 73 id: string // Unique identifier, used in expressions as $vars.{id} 74 direction: "in" | "out" | "inout" 75 type?: string // "string" (default), "number", "boolean", "object", "array", "file" 76 subType?: string // Item type for arrays (e.g., "object", "string") 77 schema?: object // JSON Schema (draft-07) for complex types 78 defaultValue?: unknown // Initial value (must match type) 79 description?: string // Human-readable description 80 triggerNodeId?: string // Trigger node this input is associated with (works in both root flows and subflows) 81 } 82 ``` 83 84 ### Examples 85 86 **String input with default:** 87 ```json 88 { 89 "id": "customerName", 90 "direction": "in", 91 "type": "string", 92 "defaultValue": "Unknown", 93 "description": "Name of the customer to process" 94 } 95 ``` 96 97 **Number output:** 98 ```json 99 { 100 "id": "totalAmount", "items": { 130 "type": "array", 131 "items": { "type": "object" } 132 } 133 }, 134 "additionalProperties": false 135 } 136 } 137 ``` 138 139 **Array with subType:** 140 ```json 141 { 142 "id": "emailList", 143 "direction": "in", 144 "type": "array", 145 "subType": "string", 146 "defaultValue": ["admin@example.com"] 147 } 148 ``` 149 150 **Input associated with a trigger:** 151 ```json 152 { 153 "id": "webhookPayload", 154 "direction": "in", 155 "type": "object", 156 "triggerNodeId": "start" 157 } 158 ``` 159 Accessed in expressions as `$vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id}` (the variable is nested under the trigger node's output — NOT `$vars.{id}`). 160 161 162 **File input (`type: "file"`):** 163 ```json 164 { 165 "id": "inputDoc", 166 "direction": "in", 167 "type": "file", 168 "description": "Document uploaded at trigger / bound via --attachment", 169 "triggerNodeId": "start" 170 } 171 ``` 172 173 > **Runtime shape of a `file` variable.** At runtime a `file` variable is an **object** (the *Flow Attachment* object), not a string. A Script node reading `$vars.start.output.inputDoc` receives: 174 > 175 > ```json 176 > { "ID": "", "FullName": "report.pdf", "MimeType": "application/pdf", "Metadata": { "size": "1024" } } 177 > ``` 178 > 179 > The uploaded file's name is **`.FullName`**. Property access is **case-sensitive** at runtime — these exact casings resolve, others return `undefined`/`null`: `.ID` (uppercase, not `.Id`), `.FullName`, `.MimeType`, and the **nested `.Metadata.size`** (lowercase `size`, NOT `.Size`). `.name` / `.fileName` do **not** exist. Two layers: the `.flow` *declaration* is camelCase (`type`, `direction`); the *runtime* object carries the casing above. Do NOT write `"FullName"` into the `.flow` source. Bind the file with `uip maestro flow debug --attachment =` — see [cli-commands.md — Pre-flight](cli-commands.md#attachment-preflight). 180 181 ### Type Reference 182 183 | Type | Default Value | Notes | 184 | --- | --- | --- | 185 | `string` | `""` | Default type if omitted | 186 | `number` | `0` | Integer or float | 187 | `boolean` | `false` | | 188 | `object` | `{}` | Use `schema` for structured objects | 189 | `array` | `[]` | Use `subType` for typed arrays | 190 | `file` | — | Bound at runtime via `--attachment`; hydrates as an object — read `.FullName` (see [File input](#file-input) above) | 191 192 --- 193 194 ## Node Variables (`nodes`) 195 196 Node variables represent outputs produced by nodes during execution. They are read-only and referenced via `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}`. 197 198 When you add a node via `uip maestro flow node add`, node variables are created automatically. When using `Edit` against the `.flow` file, add them manually. 199 200 ### Schema 201 202 ```typescript 203 { 204 id: string // Format: "{nodeId}.{outputId}" 205 type?: string // Output type 206 subType?: string // For complex types 207 schema?: object // JSON Schema for structured outputs 208 description?: string // What this output contains 209 binding: { 210 nodeId: string // Source node ID 211 outputId: string // Output port ID (e.g., "output", "error") 212 } 213 } 214 ``` 215 216 ### Example 217 218 ```json 219 { 220 "variables": { 221 "nodes": [ 222 { 223 "id": "fetchData.output", 224 "type": "object", 225 "description": "HTTP response body", 226 "binding": { 227 "nodeId": "fetchData", 228 "outputId": "output" 229 } 230 }, 231 { 232 "id": "fetchData.error", 233 "type": "object", 234 "description": "Error details if the request fails", 235 "schema": { 236 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", 237 "type": "object", 238 "required": ["code", "message"], 239 "properties": { 240 "code": { "type": "string" }, 241 "message": { "type": "string" }, 242 "detail": { "type": "string" }, 243 "category": { "type": "string" }, 244 "status": { "type": "integer" } 245 } 246 }, 247 "binding": { 248 "nodeId": "fetchData", 249 "outputId": "error" 250 } 251 } 252 ] 253 } 254 } 255 ``` 256 257 --- 258 259 ## Variable Updates (`variableUpdates`) 260 261 Variable updates assign new values to `inout` (state) variables at specific nodes. They execute when the node completes. 262 263 ### Schema 264 265 ```typescript 266 { 267 "variableUpdates": { 268 "{nodeId}": [ 269 { 270 "variableId": string, // ID of the inout variable to update 271 "expression": string // =js: expression to evaluate and assign 272 } 273 ] 274 } 275 } 276 ``` 277 278 ### Example 279 280 ```json 281 { 282 "variables": { 283 "globals": [ 284 { 285 "id": "counter", 286 "direction": "inout", 287 "type": "number", 288 "defaultValue": 0 289 }, 290 { 291 "id": "lastStatus", 292 "direction": "inout", 293 "type": "string", 294 "defaultValue": "pending" 295 } 296 ], 297 "variableUpdates": { 298 "processItem": [ 299 { 300 "variableId": "counter", 301 "expression": "=js:$vars.counter + 1" 302 }, 303 { 304 "variableId": "lastStatus", 305 "expression": "=js:$vars.processItem.output.status" 306 } 307 ] 308 } 309 } 310 } 311 ``` 312 313 > **Only `inout` variables can be updated.** Updating an `in` or `out` variable is invalid. 314 315 > **Inside loops:** variableUpdate expressions cannot access loop iteration variables like `$vars..currentItem`. Those are only available inside the body node's script. The variableUpdate must reference the body node's output (e.g., `=js:$vars.bodyNode.output`). 316 317 --- 318 319 ## Output Mapping on End Nodes 320 321 Workflow output variables (`direction: "out"`) must be mapped on End nodes. The End node's `outputs` object maps each output variable ID to a source expression. 322 323 ### Structure 324 325 ```json 326 { 327 "id": "end1", 328 "type": "core.control.end", 329 "typeVersion": "1.0", 330 "display": { "label": "End" }, 331 "inputs": {}, 332 "outputs": { 333 "totalAmount": { 334 "source": "=js:$vars.calculateTotal.output.amount" 335 }, 336 "summary": { 337 "source": "=js:$vars.formatResult.output.text" 338 } 339 } 340 } 341 ``` 342 343 > **Every `out` variable must have a mapping on every End node** that the flow can reach. Missing mappings cause runtime errors. 344 345 --- 346 347 ## Expression System 348 349 Flow uses a **Jint-based JavaScript engine** (ES2020 subset) for expressions. There are two expression formats. 350 351 ### `=js:` Expressions (Full JavaScript) 352 353 Used for conditions, input values, variable updates, and output mappings. The `=js:` prefix tells the engine to evaluate the rest as JavaScript. 354 355 ``` 356 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.status === "approved" 357 ``` 358 359 ### Template Expressions (`{ }`) 360 361 Used for string interpolation in **native flow string fields** only. Expressions inside single braces are evaluated and converted to strings. 362 363 ``` 364 Order {$vars.orderId} is {$vars.status} — total: {$vars.amount} 365 ``` 366 367 > **Brace-templates do NOT work in Integration Service activity inputs.** The flow-layer template runner only processes native flow fields (decision expressions, variable updates, end-node output `source`, script bodies, agent prompt text). Fields inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` on `core.action.http.v2` or `uipath.connector.*` activity nodes — `url`, `headers`, `body`, `query` — are passed through to the IS runtime unchanged, so `{$vars.article}` ships literally. Observed behavior: the `$` is stripped and the braces survive (`user/{vars.article}` reaches the service). **For any dynamic value in an IS activity input, use `=js:` instead** — e.g., `` "url": "=js:`https://.../user/${$vars.article}`" `` or `"headers": { "Authorization": "=js:'Bearer ' + $vars.token" }`. 368 369 ### IS Activity Inputs Require `=js:` (Critical) 370 371 Every `$vars` / `$metadata` / `$self` reference inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters`, `inputs.detail.queryParameters`, or `inputs.detail.pathParameters` on a connector or HTTP activity node MUST be wrapped with `=js:`. Without it the value ships as a literal string at runtime. 372 373 | Wrong | Right | 374 |---|---| 375 | `"recordId": "$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 376 | `"recordId": "nodes.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 377 | `"recordId": "{vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id}"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 378 | `"recordId": "=js:createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 379 380 The serializer rewrites `$vars` → `vars` whether or not `=js:` is present, so a missing prefix yields a confusing failure: the runtime field is bound to the literal string `"vars.X.output.Id"` (which looks like an unevaluated expression). The last row above is the opposite mistake — `=js:` is present but the `$vars.` prefix on the node reference is missing, so the expression evaluates a bare (undefined) identifier instead of the node's output. `flow validate` catches this (cli-side `expression-prefix-validator`, error with remediation hint) — older cli versions without the validator still let it through to `flow debug`. See [node-output-wiring.md](node-output-wiring.md) for the full per-node-type field reference (MST-9107). 381 382 ### Comparison 383 384 | Feature | `=js:` | `{ }` template | 385 | --- | --- | --- | 386 | Return type | Any (boolean, number, object, array) | Always string | 387 | Use case | Conditions, inputs, mappings | Native flow text/prompt fields only | 388 | Works in IS activity inputs (HTTP URL/headers/body, connector `bodyParameters`) | Yes | **No — use `=js:`** | 389 | Full JS | Yes | Expression-only (no statements) | 390 | Prefix | `=js:` required | No prefix, braces inline | 391 392 --- 393 394 ## Available Globals 395 396 These variables are available in all expression contexts: 397 398 | Global | Description | Access pattern | 399 | --- | --- | --- | 400 | `$vars` | All workflow and node variables | `$vars.{variableId}` or `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}` | 401 | `$metadata` | Workflow metadata (instanceId, executionId) | `$metadata.instanceId` | 402 | `$self` | Current node's output (HTTP branch conditions only) | `$self.output.statusCode` | 403 | `$vars..*` | Loop iteration context (inside loops only) | `$vars.loop1.currentItem`, `$vars.loop1.currentIndex` | 404 405 ### `$vars` Access Patterns 406 407 ```javascript 408 // Workflow global 409 $vars.customerName 410 $vars.counter 411 412 // Trigger-associated flow input (triggerNodeId set) 413 $vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id} 414 415 // File input (type: "file") → object, read .FullName for the name 416 $vars.start.output.inputDoc.FullName 417 418 // Node output (script node) 419 $vars.script1.output 420 $vars.script1.output.someField 421 422 // Node output (HTTP node) 423 $vars.fetchData.output.body 424 $vars.fetchData.output.statusCode 425 $vars.fetchData.output.headers 426 427 // Node error 428 $vars.fetchData.error.message 429 $vars.fetchData.error.code 430 ``` 431 432 --- 433 434 ## Expression Contexts 435 436 Expressions behave differently depending on where they appear. 437 438 ### Script Node Body 439 440 The `inputs.script` field contains a function body. Full JavaScript statements are allowed (variables, loops, conditionals). The returned value becomes `$vars.{nodeId}.output`. 441 442 Scripts can return any value — objects, numbers, strings, arrays, or booleans: 443 444 ```javascript 445 // Returning an object (multiple fields) 446 const items = $vars.fetchData.output.body.items; 447 const filtered = items.filter(i => i.active); 448 return { count: filtered.length, names: filtered.map(i => i.name) }; 449 450 // Returning a bare value (useful for accumulators in loops) 451 return $vars.total + $vars.loop1.currentItem; 452 ``` 453 454 ### Decision Node (`inputs.expression`) 455 456 A single boolean expression. Result is coerced to `Boolean()`. 457 458 ``` 459 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.verified === true 460 ``` 461 462 Determines which port fires: `true` or `false`. 463 464 ### Switch Node (`inputs.cases[].expression`) 465 466 Each case has an expression evaluated in order. First truthy result wins; otherwise the `default` port fires. 467 468 ```json 469 { 470 "inputs": { 471 "cases": [ 472 { "label": "Low", "expression": "$vars.score <= 30" }, 473 { "label": "Medium", "expression": "$vars.score <= 70" }, 474 { "label": "High", "expression": "$vars.score > 70" } 475 ] 476 } 477 } 478 ``` 479 480 ### HTTP Branch Condition (`inputs.branches[].conditionExpression`) 481 482 Uses `$self` to reference the current HTTP node's response. 483 484 ``` 485 $self.output.statusCode >= 200 && $self.output.statusCode < 300 486 ``` 487 488 ### Variable Update Expressions 489 490 Evaluate to the new value for the target variable. 491 492 ``` 493 =js:$vars.counter + 1 494 =js:$vars.items.concat([$vars.newItem.output]) 495 ``` 496 497 ### Loop Collection Expression 498 499 The `inputs.collection` field on a Loop node resolves to an array to iterate over. 500 501 ``` 502 =js:$vars.fetchData.output.body.items 503 =js:$vars.inputArray.filter(x => x.active) 504 ``` 505 506 Inside the loop body, use `$vars..currentItem` and `$vars..currentIndex` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`). 507 508 --- 509 510 ## Jint Engine Constraints 511 512 The production runtime uses **Jint** (a .NET JavaScript interpreter, ES2020 subset). Key constraints: 513 514 ### Supported 515 516 - Arithmetic: `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `%` 517 - Comparison: `===`, `!==`, `==`, `!=`, `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=` 518 - Logical: `&&`, `||`, `!` 519 - Ternary: `condition ? a : b` 520 - String methods: `.toUpperCase()`, `.toLowerCase()`, `.trim()`, `.split()`, `.includes()`, `.startsWith()`, `.slice()`, `.substring()` 521 - Array methods: `.filter()`, `.map()`, `.reduce()`, `.find()`, `.some()`, `.every()`, `.concat()`, `.length` 522 - Object: `Object.keys()`, `Object.values()`, `Object.entries()` 523 - Math: `Math.floor()`, `Math.ceil()`, `Math.round()`, `Math.abs()`, `Math.min()`, `Math.max()`, `Math.random()` 524 - JSON: `JSON.parse()`, `JSON.stringify()` 525 - Template literals: `` `Hello ${name}` `` 526 - Destructuring: `const { a, b } = obj` (in script bodies) 527 - Spread operator: `[...arr1, ...arr2]` (in script bodies) 528 - Arrow functions: `items.filter(x => x.active)` (inline callbacks) 529 530 ### Not Supported 531 532 - `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `setTimeout`, `setInterval` — no network or timers 533 - `document`, `window`, `console` — no DOM or browser globals 534 - `require`, `import` — no module system 535 - `eval`, `Function` constructor — no dynamic code generation 536 - `async`/`await`, `Promise` — no async operations 537 - `Date` constructor may have limited support — prefer ISO 8601 strings 538 539 > **When in doubt, keep expressions simple.** Complex data processing should go in Script nodes where you have full statement support, not in one-line expressions. 540 541 --- 542 543 ## Scoping Rules 544 545 ### Node Output Availability 546 547 A node's output (`$vars.{nodeId}.output`) is available to **all downstream nodes** connected via edges. If a node has not executed (e.g., on an untaken branch), its `$vars` entry is `undefined`. 548 549 ### Loop Scope 550 551 Inside a loop body, you have access to: 552 - All parent-scope `$vars` (read-only from loop's perspective) 553 - `$vars..currentItem` — current array element 554 - `$vars..currentIndex` — zero-based index 555 - `$vars..collection` — the original array 556 557 Where `` is the loop node's `id` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`). 558 559 > **Important:** Loop body nodes must have `"parentId": ""` set in their JSON. Without this, the runtime does not know the node is inside the loop and `$vars..currentItem` will be undefined. 560 561 After loop completion, `$vars..output` contains aggregated results from all iterations. 562 563 ### Subflow Scope 564 565 Subflows have their own variable scope. Parent variables are **not** automatically visible inside a subflow. Pass values explicitly via subflow `inputs` and receive results via subflow `outputs`. 566 567 --- 568 569 ## Variable Management via CLI 570 571 There are **no CLI commands** for adding or removing variables. Manage variables with `Edit` against the `.flow` file. 572 573 ### Adding a workflow input variable 574 575 1. Open `.flow` 576 2. Add the variable object to `variables.globals` 577 3. Run `uip maestro flow validate` to check for errors 578 579 ### Adding node variables after manual node insertion 580 581 When adding nodes via `Edit` (not CLI), you must also add corresponding entries to `variables.nodes`: 582 583 ```json 584 { 585 "id": "myScript.output", 586 "type": "object", 587 "binding": { "nodeId": "myScript", "outputId": "output" } 588 }, 589 { 590 "id": "myScript.error", 591 "type": "object", 592 "binding": { "nodeId": "myScript", "outputId": "error" } 593 } 594 ``` 595 596 > **When using `uip maestro flow node add`**, node variables are handled automatically. Only add them manually when using `Edit` against the `.flow` file. 597 598 ### Mapping outputs on End nodes 599 600 For every `out` variable, add a mapping in each End node's `outputs`: 601 602 ```json 603 "outputs": { 604 "result": { 605 "source": "=js:$vars.processData.output" 606 } 607 } 608 ``` 609 610 --- 611 612 ## Complete Example 613 614 A flow with input, state, and output 1	# CLI Conventions
2	
3	Shared conventions for the `uip` CLI that apply across **all three capabilities** (Author, Operate, Diagnose). Read this first when invoking any `uip` command — every capability assumes these mechanics.
4	
5	## 1. Resolve the `uip` binary and detect command prefix
6	
7	The `uip` CLI is installed via npm. Resolve the binary (it may not be on PATH in nvm environments) and detect the command namespace.
8	
9	```bash
10	UIP=$(command -v uip 2>/dev/null || echo "$(npm root -g 2>/dev/null | sed 's|/node_modules$||')/bin/uip")
11	CURRENT=$($UIP --version 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $NF}')
12	```
13	
14	If `uip` is not found at all, install it:
15	
16	```bash
17	npm install -g @uipath/cli@latest
18	```
19	
20	If `npm install -g` fails with a permission error, prompt the user to re-run with appropriate privileges — do not retry automatically.
21	
22	### Command prefix by version
23	
24	| Installed version | Command prefix | Example |
25	| --- | --- | --- |
26	| **≥ 0.3.4** | `uip maestro flow` | `uip maestro flow init MyProject` |
27	| **< 0.3.4** | `uip flow` | `uip flow init MyProject` <!-- uip-check-skip --> |
28	
29	```bash
30	MIN_VERSION="0.3.4"
31	if [ "$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$MIN_VERSION" "$CURRENT" | sort -V | head -n1)" = "$MIN_VERSION" ]; then
32	  FLOW_CMD="uip maestro flow"
33	else
34	  FLOW_CMD="uip flow" # <!-- uip-check-skip -->  legacy < 0.3.4 prefix
35	fi
36	echo "Using: $FLOW_CMD (CLI version $CURRENT)"
37	```
38	
39	> **All commands across this skill are written as `uip maestro flow ...` (the ≥ 0.3.4 form).** If version detection above returns < 0.3.4, replace `uip maestro flow` with `uip flow`. Arguments and flags are identical — only the prefix differs. See UiPath/cli#841 for background on the restructuring. <!-- uip-check-skip -->
40	
41	## 2. Always use `--output json`
42	
43	All `uip` commands support structured JSON output. Use `--output json` whenever output is parsed programmatically — every reference doc and recipe in this skill assumes it.
44	
45	```bash
46	uip maestro flow validate <ProjectName>.flow --output json
47	uip maestro flow registry list --output json
48	uip maestro flow instance incidents <INSTANCE_ID> --folder-key <FOLDER_KEY> --output json
49	```
50	
51	> **Anti-pattern: `--format json` does NOT exist.** The flag is `--output json`. Using `--format json` produces `error: unknown option '--format'` and exit code 3 on every `uip` subcommand — not a helpful message pointing at `--output`.
52	
53	The `--localstorage-file` warning that appears in some environments is benign and can be ignored.
54	
55	## 3. Prefer `--output-filter` for extraction
56	
57	When extracting one field or a projection from `uip --output json`, use `--output-filter '<jmespath>'`. The CLI exposes `--output-filter <expression>` as a global flag on every subcommand; it applies a [JMESPath](https://jmespath.org/) expression to the `Data` envelope **before** printing. Write expressions starting at `Data` — do **not** prefix them with `Data.`.

Create a UiPath Flow project named "WikiPageviews" that takes `article`
(string) and `date1`, `date2` (strings in `YYYYMMDD` format) as inputs.
Fetch the daily view counts in the range from the Wikimedia pageviews API
(`https://wikimedia.org/api/rest_v1/metrics/pageviews/per-article/en.wikipedia/all-access/user/{article}/daily/{date1}/{date2}`)
in a single call. Preserve every constant path segment of that URL
verbatim — including the literal `/daily/` between `{article}` and
`{date1}` — and only substitute the three placeholders; dropping any
segment makes the route invalid and Wikimedia returns 404. The request
must include a descriptive `User-Agent` header (e.g.
`WikiPageviewsFlow/1.0 (example@example.com)`) — Wikimedia rejects
requests without one (HTTP 403 per their robot policy).

Express the data pipeline as two distinct steps: first keep only the days
whose `views` exceed 500, then aggregate the surviving `views` into a
single integer total — pick the right Flow node for each step rather than
collapsing both into one. When the upstream call fails (e.g. the article
does not exist and the API returns an error), the flow must instead
return the literal string `Article not found`.

Do NOT ask for approval, confirmation, or feedback. Do NOT pause between planning and implementation. Build the complete flow end-to-end in a single pass.
